title: Left exactness of finite-free constant scalar extension at independent universes
statement:
Let C be a category essentially small in a coefficient universe r, J a Grothendieck topology, and A → B a unital map of commutative rings in r with B finite free over A. Assume weak sheafification of commutative rings and left exact sheafification of abelian groups, with local bijectivity detecting its equivalences. Constant ring sheaves are [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and module sheaves are [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. If E is the specified sheafified extension of scalars [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], with its actual object and morphism equations, then E preserves finite limits. The object and morphism universes of C are independent of r.

theorem CategoryTheory.constantFiniteFree_extensionLeftExact
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [EssentiallySmall.{r} C]
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) [HasWeakSheafify J CommRingCat.{r}]
    [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ CommRingCat.{r} RingCat.{r})]
    [HasSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{r}] [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{r}]
    (A B : CommRingCat.{r}) [Algebra A B] [Module.Finite A B] [Module.Free A B]
    (E : modules (constantRing J A) ⥤ modules (constantRing J B))
    (h : ∀ M, E.obj M = SheafOfModules.changeOfRings
      ((constantSheaf J CommRingCat.{r}).map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A B))) M)
    (hm : ∀ {M N} (f : M ⟶ N), E.map f = eqToHom (h M) ≫
      SheafOfModules.changeOfRingsHom
        ((constantSheaf J CommRingCat.{r}).map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A B)))
          M f ≫ eqToHom (h N).symm) : PreservesFiniteLimits E

proof.text: Choose a finite basis of B over A. Regard its coordinate isomorphism as an isomorphism of constant module presheaves, then apply module sheafification along the unit of the constant A-ring sheaf. The map to the restricted regular constant B-module is an isomorphism: after forgetting to abelian sheaves, its composite with the sheafification unit is the constant B-ring sheafification unit, which is locally bijective. Module sheafification preserves finite products, so this constructs a finite-power isomorphism for the restricted constant B-module. Evaluating it gives a basis on every site object whose coordinates commute with restrictions. This is the private basisConstruct proof of ConstantFiniteFreeSectionBasis generalized using EssentiallySmall at the coefficient universe; no maximum-of-universes assumption is introduced.

On each section module, use the basis tensor equivalence B(U) tensor M(U) ≃ M(U)^n. Its naturality follows from the coordinate restriction formula and tensor induction. The inverse formulas give a presheaf isomorphism. Sheafify it; the finite power of the underlying abelian presheaf of M is already a sheaf, so its sheafification unit is invertible. The existing proved private helpers sheafifiedTensorIso and sheafifiedTensorIso_naturality in ConstantFiniteFreePowerIso carry out exactly this calculation at independent universes. The object and map equations for E then produce a natural finite-power isomorphism for its underlying abelian presheaf functor.

The underlying abelian presheaf functor preserves finite limits. The finite-power functor is a composite of a constant-diagram functor and a limit functor, hence preserves finite limits. Transport preservation across the natural isomorphism and use reflection of finite limits by the target underlying-presheaf functor. Empty finite powers are included, so rank zero requires no separate hypothesis.
